_note: Week of Nov. 16 capsules, written from the frozen fact sheet in 2026-11-16.json.
miami-oh:
The RedHawks have played three games and two of them in other people's buildings, which in November is either bravery or scheduling, and the Bricks Index does not much care which. It pays for the address. Miami won at James Madison 86-77 on the second night of the season and at Evansville 86-78 on Saturday, the same 86 both times, as if the offense had set a thermostat and walked away from it.

That is the case for No. 1, and it is a case built on travel. Recent form has Miami at plus-3.8 points a game against an average team, good but not the best in the league. The two road wins add another 1.2, and the sum, plus-5.1, is the top figure in the MAC this week. Akron is better by the model alone. Miami is better by the miles.

The scoring has no single owner. Almar Atlason, a senior forward, and Luke Skaljac, a junior guard, are both at 14 points a game, and Skaljac has added seven assists a night in his two appearances, the number of a player who reads a defense the way a cartographer reads a coastline. Stevie Elam, a sophomore guard, is at 13.7 with 5.7 rebounds, the kind of line that fills a box score from the edges in.

Three players within half a point of one another is either a balanced team or an unsettled one, and three games is not enough to say which. The good news for Miami is that it does not have to decide yet.

The week ahead is gentler. Defiance, a non-Division I visitor, comes in Wednesday, and on Sunday the RedHawks meet UIC on a neutral floor, a game that counts half on the road ledger and double in the argument. The ranking rewards the team that leaves home and comes back with something. Miami keeps packing.
akron:
Akron has not lost, and in the Bricks Index that is not quite enough, which tells you something about the Index and something about the week. The Zips beat Muskingum 112-64 on Monday and Tulane 65-63 on Saturday, both at home, and home wins earn nothing beyond what the model already sees.

The model sees plenty: plus-4.3 points a game in recent form, the best in the MAC. What it does not see is a fresh road win. The one from Lafayette, 75-61 over Louisiana on Nov. 2, is two weeks old and fading on schedule, worth 0.3 now. Add it up and Akron sits at plus-4.6, a half-step behind Miami.

The Tulane game was the one with a pulse. Muskingum, a non-Division I opponent, could tell you only that the Zips can count past 100. Tulane, two points from the end, asked whether they could close, and they answered.

The scoring has two heads. Tahj Staveskie and Ty Pence, both senior guards, are at 16.3 points a game apiece, Staveskie shooting like a man who has somewhere to be, Pence pulling down six rebounds a night, which is a guard doing a forward's work without filing a complaint. Evan Mahaffey, the senior forward, is at 11.3 points, 6.3 rebounds and 4.3 assists, the line of a player who keeps the other two supplied and asks nothing for it.

Which brings the week into focus, because the week is the thing. Akron goes to Bucknell on Tuesday, a true road game, the kind the Index was built to reward and the only one on the calendar. WVU Tech, a non-Division I visitor, follows on Friday.

Win in Lewisburg and the gap closes. The Zips have the best engine in the league. They need only to drive it somewhere.
toledo:
Toledo's record says 2-3, the Bricks Index says third in the MAC, and the distance between those two statements is the whole idea of the thing. The Rockets have lost more than they have won. They have also won twice away from home, at Marshall 81-76 on Nov. 7 and at Detroit Mercy 85-72 on Saturday, and no team in the league carries more road credit this week. Those wins are worth 1.7 points a game on top of a recent form of plus-2.7. The sum, plus-4.4, sits a whisker behind Akron.

The week split down the middle. Wright State came to Toledo on Tuesday and left with a 76-68 win, the kind of evening a home crowd files away without comment. Four days later the Rockets drove to Detroit and scored 85, which is how you answer a home loss: somewhere else, and loudly.

Mynor Strong, a junior guard, is the reason the answers come. He is averaging 17.8 points over five games, the most of any Rocket and steady enough to be mistaken for a schedule. Jaylan Ouwinga, a junior forward, adds 13.4 points and 6.8 rebounds, doing the inside work that lets Strong drift outside. Angel Montas Jr., a senior guard, is at 10.6 points and 4.8 rebounds, a third option who plays like a first one when asked.

There is a temptation to call Toledo's record misleading, and it would be wrong. The losses happened. What the Index argues is that they are not the most interesting thing about this team, that the miles say more than the margin.

One game this week: Robert Morris at home on Thursday. A win there moves no road needle, but it keeps the form number climbing. Toledo has shown it can win in other people's gyms. Now it would like to win one in front of its own people.
western-michigan:
Western Michigan has won four straight, the last two on the road and both by the kind of margin that makes the bus ride home a pleasant one: 81-59 at Purdue Fort Wayne on Thursday, 80-59 at Southern Indiana on Sunday. Twenty-two and twenty-one. The Broncos are not winning close games because they are not playing any.

The Index is a touch more reserved about it. The road ledger lists the Fort Wayne win this week, at 0.4 points a game, and recent form carries the rest: plus-2.2 against an average team, fourth in the MAC. The total is plus-2.6, and it is a total that looks like a team gathering speed rather than one that has arrived.

What the box scores flatter is the distribution. Augustinas Kiudulas, a senior forward, leads at 12.8 points and 5.4 rebounds. Rob Lee Jr., a senior guard, is at 12.4 with 5.8 rebounds, a guard who goes after the ball as if he has been told it belongs to him. Jaylen Washington, a junior guard, adds 11.8 points and 3.8 assists. Three players separated by a single point. It is a roster that does not need a hero, which is the best kind to have in November, when heroes are still learning their lines.

The one loss on the record came in the opener, before this run began, and the run has been long enough to make it feel like a rumor. Four wins since, two of them out of state, and a plus-21 or better in each of the last two.

Friday the Broncos go east to Mount St. Mary's, the only game on the week's card and another one in somebody else's gym. If the pattern holds, Western Michigan will treat it like the last two: arrive early, take care of business, and leave the margin up on the scoreboard for the locals to think about on the drive home.
bowling-green:
Bowling Green is 3-0, has scored 95 and 88 in its two home games, and sits fifth, which is less an insult than a description of what the Bricks Index chooses to notice. It notices the road. The Falcons' only road win, 76-73 at Georgia State on the second night of the season, was a close and honest one, and two weeks on it is worth 0.6 points a game. Recent form adds 1.4. Plus-2.1 in all.

The home week was a lively one. Cleveland State came down on Monday and lost 95-79. Niagara came in on Thursday and lost 88-76. Both were evenings in which the Falcons simply had more of the ball go in, which is the oldest strategy in the sport and still undefeated.

The guards have it. Makhi Leach, a sophomore, is at 17.7 points and 5.7 assists, the line of a player who runs the show and stars in it at the same time. Zach Howell, a senior, adds 16.7 points and six rebounds. Josiah Shackelford, a junior, is at 15.7 with 6.3 rebounds and 3.3 assists. Three guards scoring more than fifteen a night and all of them rebounding: it is a backcourt that does not wait for the big men to do the dirty work, because it has decided the dirty work is the fun part.

There is a version of this team that is a little too comfortable at home, and the Index exists to ask whether that version is the real one. Three games is not an answer. It is barely a question.

The week poses it directly. Tuesday is a trip to William & Mary, a road game the Index will pay for if the Falcons bring it home. Saturday, Northern Illinois, an old MAC neighbor, visits. If Leach and company can carry their scoring across state lines, fifth will not hold them long.
central-michigan:
Central Michigan is 4-0 and has spent the early season collecting road wins in places the MAC does not often visit: 83-78 at UL Monroe on Nov. 2 and 68-57 at Northern Kentucky on Saturday. Together they are worth 0.7 points a game, the same as the Chippewas' recent form. Plus-1.4 overall, sixth in the league, and an unbeaten record that has been earned the hard way, at least half of it in someone else's building.

The home win came Tuesday, 91-78 over Youngstown State, a game in which the Chippewas scored the way teams score when one man has the ball and the others have learned to get out of his way.

That man is Phat Phat Brooks, a junior guard, who is averaging 21 points a game, the highest figure in the MAC, with four assists to go with it. It is a name that sounds like an announcer's dream and a stat line that reads like a scout's. Conrad Luczynski, a senior center, adds 11.2 points and 7.2 rebounds, the ballast in the hull. Jalen Kampen, a sophomore guard, is at an even 10.

There are teams that ease into November and teams that are thrown into it. Central Michigan's calendar has chosen for it. Tuesday the Chippewas play at Dayton. Friday they play at Pittsburgh. Two road games in four days against the kind of opponents the Index pays well for, and the kind of week that tells a team who it is before it has had time to decide for itself.

Lose both and nobody will be surprised, least of all the formula, which knows exactly what a road game at a place like Dayton costs. Win one and the Index will notice in a hurry. This is a ranking that rewards the brave. Central Michigan did not pick this week. It only has to survive it.
ohio:
Ohio has a road win and a road loss, and the Bricks Index is built so that the first one counts for more than the second one costs. The win came on Nov. 2 at South Alabama, 86-77, and even two weeks later it is worth 0.9 points a game, the second-largest single road win in the MAC this week, behind only Toledo's at Marshall. The loss came Friday at Purdue, 80-62, in a building where visitors rarely leave happy.

Recent form, which takes the Purdue game at its full weight, has the Bobcats at plus-0.1, as close to perfectly average as a team can be without a ruler. Add the road credit and Ohio is at plus-0.9, seventh in the league, with a 2-1 record that does not tell you nearly enough.

What tells you more is the roster's age. The top three scorers are seniors. Jackson Paveletzke, a guard, leads at 15.3 points and 5.3 assists, and has the look in the box score of a player who has seen most things a college defense can show him. Javan Simmons, a forward, adds 13.3 points and 5.3 rebounds. Siebe Ledegen, a guard, is at 11.0. It is a team that ought to know how to win in March, and the question November asks is whether it can find a way to win now.

The Purdue game is not the measure. Most teams that visit West Lafayette go home with a long bus ride and not much else. The South Alabama game, won by nine on the road in the season's first week, might be.

One game on the week's card: Morehead State at home on Wednesday. It will not move the road ledger. It will move the form number, and a team this experienced should know that the ranking is listening. Seniors get one more November. Ohio would be wise to use it.
umass:
UMass is 2-1, with a road win at Troy on Nov. 2, 71-60, that is still worth 0.6 points a game, and a home win over UMass Lowell on Wednesday, 72-62, in the kind of game that a state's basketball fans argue about long after the box score is filed. Recent form has the Minutemen at plus-0.1, a hair above average. The total is plus-0.7, eighth in the MAC, and a long way from settled.

The best thing about UMass so far is a senior forward named Junjie Wang, who is averaging 17.7 points and 9.3 rebounds, a near double-double every night and the kind of production that makes a coach stop drawing up plays and start drawing up ways to get him the ball. Jordan Clayton, a senior guard, adds 12.3 points. Dwayne Wimbley Jr., a sophomore forward, is at 11.3 points, eight rebounds and three assists, a young player whose numbers suggest he has already figured out where the ball is going to come down.

Wang and Wimbley together are pulling down more than 17 rebounds a game. In a league where possessions are precious and second chances are worth their weight in banners, that is not a small thing.

The week asks very little of the Minutemen on the road and a fair amount at home. Bryant visits on Tuesday and Maine on Saturday, both at the Mullins Center, both chances to push the form number up without moving the road ledger an inch.

The Bricks Index will treat both games honestly, which is to say it will care about the margin and the opponent and nothing about the crowd. That is fine. UMass has a frontcourt that wins on the glass, and the glass looks the same in every building. The miles can wait a week.
eastern-michigan:
Eastern Michigan won a road game at Coastal Carolina on Nov. 2 by a single point, 71-70, and two weeks later that one point is still holding up a ranking. The win is worth 0.4 points a game on the road ledger. Recent form has the Eagles at minus-1.5, and the sum, minus-1.1, places them ninth in the MAC.

The only game last week was a 108-44 home win over Great Lakes Christian, a non-Division I opponent, the sort of evening the model treats with polite indifference. It does not tell you much, except that everyone got to play.

What does tell you something is Mohammad Habhab. A sophomore forward, he is averaging 20.7 points and eight rebounds a game, second in the MAC only to Central Michigan's Phat Phat Brooks among the scorers we track. Twenty points a night from a sophomore is the kind of number that changes how a program thinks about the next three years. Emanuel Richards, a senior guard, is at 16.0 points and 5.5 rebounds in two games. Jaiden Martin, a junior guard, adds 12.7.

There is a shape to this team: a young forward who scores inside and a pair of guards who score outside, and enough of each to keep a defense honest. What it has not had yet is a stretch of Division I games long enough to tell the model which version of itself is the real one.

The week brings two home games against Division I opponents, and that is a gift to a team trying to prove a number wrong. Detroit Mercy comes in on Wednesday. Denver comes in on Saturday. Neither will add road credit. Both will speak loudly to the form number.

Habhab will be the headline either way. The question is whether the Eagles can make him the first sentence of the story rather than the whole thing.
kent-state:
Kent State has not won on the road yet, and in a ranking that pays for travel, that is the first fact and most of the second one. The Golden Flashes went to UNC Wilmington on Wednesday and lost 91-73, the kind of road trip that has to be survived rather than enjoyed. They are 1-2. Recent form is minus-3.0 points a game, there is no road credit to add, and the index is minus-3.0, tenth in the MAC.

None of which tells you much about where this team is going, only where it has been, and it has been to some difficult places in the season's first two weeks.

The most interesting name on the roster belongs to a freshman. Dhani Miller, a guard, is averaging 14.0 points, five rebounds and three assists in two games, and is leading the team in scoring at an age when most players are still learning the names of the plays. Chansey Willis Jr., a senior guard, adds 12.0 points and three assists. Christian Henry, another senior guard, is at 10.7.

A freshman leading a team of seniors is either a sign of trouble or a sign of hope, and November rarely says which. What can be said is that Miller's line is that of a player who is not shy about the ball, and that is a trait which tends to stay.

The week ahead offers exactly what Kent State needs: a chance. Eastern Kentucky comes to the M.A.C. Center on Monday, the day this ranking was frozen. Then on Saturday the Flashes drive up to Cleveland State, a short trip and a real road game, the first one since Wilmington and the first chance to put anything on the ledger.

Win in Cleveland and the number moves. The formula has no memory of how it felt in Wilmington. It only wants to know what happens next.
buffalo:
Buffalo has won two straight, both at home and both convincingly: 107-65 over Penn State Schuylkill, a non-Division I opponent, on Monday, and 79-55 over Canisius on Sunday, a 24-point win in a regional matchup that people in Western New York tend to take personally.

The Bricks Index is cooler about it than the crowd was. Recent form has the Bulls at minus-6.0 points a game, a figure dragged down by the two losses that opened the season, and with no road wins yet there is nothing to add. Minus-6.0, eleventh in the MAC.

That number may not hold. The Canisius game was the kind of performance a short-memory model eventually believes, and the roster has the pieces to keep producing them.

Drew Steffe, a senior guard, leads at 17.0 points, 6.5 rebounds and 4.2 assists, the all-purpose line of a player who has decided he will do whatever the possession requires. Antoine Lorick III, a senior forward, is averaging 15.8 points and exactly ten rebounds, a double-double average, which is the most dependable kind of production there is. Dylan Ducommun, a sophomore guard, adds 11.8 points.

Steffe and Lorick together are the sort of senior pairing that can carry a team through the long middle of a season, when the novelty has worn off and the schedule has not.

The week holds one game, and it is the right one. Buffalo goes to St. Bonaventure on Thursday, a road trip across the Southern Tier to play a neighbor, and the first chance this season to put a road win on the ledger. A win there would be worth more to the Index than both home blowouts put together.

The Bulls have been very good at home. Thursday is about finding out whether they travel.
ball-state:
Ball State is 1-3, and the schedule has not been in a forgiving mood. The Cardinals beat Brescia, a non-Division I opponent, 89-64 at home on Monday, then went to SMU on Friday and lost 90-65. Recent form is minus-9.3 points a game, there are no road wins to add, and the index is minus-9.3, twelfth in the MAC.

Last in a power ranking in mid-November is a weather report, not a verdict. It tells you what the conditions have been, and the conditions have included a trip to Dallas to play a team from the Atlantic Coast Conference.

The roster leans on its guards. Sean Blake, a junior, is averaging 16.0 points and 4.2 assists, and is the one player on the floor who looks most like a team's first option. Javion Guy-King, a senior, adds 13.0 points. Trey Lewis, another senior, is at 10.2. It is a backcourt with experience, which is worth something in a league where the long winter is played mostly in small gyms against people who know your plays.

There is a kind of team that loses early and learns from it and a kind that loses early and keeps losing, and four games is not enough to know which kind this is. What can be said is that Blake's numbers look like a player who has not stopped looking for his shot, and that tends to matter in February.

The week does not let up. Ball State goes to Florida State on Tuesday, another road game against another ACC opponent. It is a game the formula will price honestly: a loss costs a little, a win would be worth a great deal.

The Cardinals are not out of anything yet. They are just playing the hard part of the schedule first, and the hard part has a way of paying off later.
